what_happened: Scene layout/style 10 (stem faucet, side lever; as s7, s15). Stage 0 slow: first lever contact 116-141 moved the handle only 0.01, then ~230 steps hovering near the faucet (wrist on the backsplash, 141-368), second contact 368-395 turned it on at 387 (median 189, p90 230). Stage 1: 474-536 the gripper pushed the spout arm LEFT (-0.13 at 484, -0.46 at 536) and paused there to ~608 while the arm repositioned (548-600, wrist on the counter and sink). 609-620 a second push reached -0.520 at 617, 0.004 rad (0.2 deg) short of the 'left' threshold (-0.5236). It then pushed the spout the other way: -0.38 (644), +0.10 (684), +0.60 (708; right washed 703), and kept it at the right end +1.04..+1.12 from 772 to 900 in contact.
causal_chain: slow stage 0 (387, ~200 steps over median) -> left push reached -0.520 (617), 0.004 rad short of the threshold -> reversed and swung right (703) -> held right to 900 -> left never credited
self_recovery: none: after the near-miss it never pushed left again.
official_criterion_notes: Near-miss: the spout was swung 29.8 deg left of centre (threshold 30 deg); visually the stream had moved well toward the left, but the official zone was not entered. A 0.2-degree difference decided the episode.

packet_facts: spout angle from saved states (run/<tag>_steps.npz, column validated against packet washed_loc/spout_ori); 'left' needs <= -0.524 rad, 'right' >= +0.524: -0.46@536-608, min -0.5200@617, +0.60@708, +1.12@788

uncertain_about: Whether a faster stage 0 would have changed anything: after the near-miss the policy held the spout at right for ~200 steps without trying left again, so time was not the binding limit.
